To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the high tenacity polyamide (aramid) and the high modulus polyethylene fibers (HMPE) have the potential to replace polyester in the deep water mooring applications, but only the HMPE fiber has the potential to meet the requirements in ultra-deep waters.

high tenacity polyethylene (PE) fiber ropes are the most cost effective and the best solution for ultra deep water applications, and that the use of high tenacity polyaramide (PA) fiber ropes is not justified for ultra deep water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of high performance fibers and ropes in terms of their potential use in deep water mooring applications.
the development and application of high tenacity fibers for offshore mooring ropes and their deployment and retrieval systems.

the following: (i) Evaluation of different fiber types and their performance in deep water mooring ropes (ii) Development of a fiber performance model to predict fiber performance in deep water applications (iii) Development of an integrated rope performance model to evaluate overall rope performance (iv) Evaluation of different deployment methods and their effect on rope fatigue life (v) Cost analysis for different fiber types in terms of overall cost of mooring ropes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of high performance fiber for ultra deep water mooring ropes is a very viable option.
there is no single fiber that is best for all applications and all mooring systems.
the high tenacity polyaramids and high performance polyethylene are superior to polyester and other high performance fibers in terms of tenacity, modulus, creep, and abrasion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the high performance fibers have the potential to be a viable solution for deep water mooring applications.

the high performance fibers (aramid, carbon and ultra-high modulus polyethylene) have a much higher cost than polyester and are only suitable for ultra-deepwater (above 1500 meters) where the cost of a polyester rope is prohibitive due to the large rope diameter required for the same strength as a high performance fiber rope.

the performance of high modulus and high tenacity polyethylene (PE) and aramid (Kevlar) fibers is comparable to polyester (PET) in terms of tenacity and stiffness but the cost of these fibers is significantly higher.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of high tenacity polyethylene (PE) fiber is the best choice for deep water offshore applications in terms of mechanical properties, cost and lifetime performance.
high performance fibers such as PBO and HMPE have higher costs and are more difficult to handle during deployment but can offer significant cost savings for ultra-deep water mooring ropes.
the cost of the fiber is a small part of the total cost of a rope.
